paragraphs.text: DSH plugin: pick the chat language, keep code, docs and commits in en-US.
# language-plugin-dsh
Pin the language of the chat and of the artifacts in DSH — terminal and web.
Two independent axes, both enforced from a system-prompt section:
| Axis | Values | Meaning |

| `chat` | `inherit` (default), `auto`, `off`, a BCP-47 tag | the prose the agent replies with |
| `
artifacts` | `en-US` (default), `inherit`, `off`, a BCP-47 tag | everything written into a file or t

o a forge |
| `decide` | `auto` (default), `stopwords`, `jev`, `off` | how the guards judge a langua

forge |
| `decide` | `auto` (default), `stopwords`, `jev`, `off` | how the guards judge a language |

`chat` defaults to `inherit`: the reply follows the language the user writes.
`auto` is an accepted

alias for it. `artifacts` is pinned to `en-US` by
default, so identifiers, comments, documentation,

commit messages and PR bodies
are always English whatever the reply language is. `/lang` opens a num

bered
picker, and a pick typed straight into the composer is swallowed (nothing is
sent to the model

red
picker, and a pick typed straight into the composer is swallowed (nothing is
sent to the model).

- **Plugin-only.** No dsh core change, no patch, no fork. Plain Cordis services.
- **Scoped.** The c

hat rule belongs to the root agent, so a delegated child does
not inherit the user-facing voice. The

artifact rule is global: a child gets
the artifact section, an artifact-only tail reminder, and the

same write
guard, with its own budget.
- **Zero dependencies.** Plain ESM, no build step, no networ

k call.
- **Offline guard.** Optional strict mode detects an ignored chat language with a
local stop

word heuristic and steers one correction. No model call.
- **Layered.** A tail reminder rides the ru

ntime-context snapshot, a write guard
blocks artifacts that land in the wrong language, and the comp

action summary
and session title are pinned to the policy.

## Usage
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The picker lists 79 languages by number (the first ten are the most common, the rest follow alphabet
ically). Labels are the English names from `Intl.DisplayNames`; the status line carries the tag. Key
ally). Labels are the English names from `Intl.DisplayNames`; the status line carries the tag. Keys:
| Key | Action |

| `1`-`79` | set the chat language |
| `0` | follow the user (`inherit`) |
| `o` | chat off |
| `s`

| toggle strict |
| `q` | close the picker |

The picker closes on any other message, which then goes through normally. It
expires after 120 s. A

language outside the list is set by tag
(`/lang chat eo`). Language tags are canonicalized (`pt-br`

becomes `pt-BR`)
and validated with `Intl.getCanonicalLocales`; anything that is not a tag is
reject

omes `pt-BR`)
and validated with `Intl.getCanonicalLocales`; anything that is not a tag is
rejected.

State lives in `~/.config/language-plugin-dsh/config.json` (0700 directory,
0600 file, atomic write)

. The file is the runtime truth; the row config in
`cordis.patch.yml` only seeds a fresh install.
## Deciders
The guards need to know which language a text is in.
| Mode | Behaviour |
| `auto` | offline for the six languages the local detector knows, the decision model for anything e

lse |
| `stopwords` | always offline |
| `jev` | always the model, with the offline detector as fall

back |
| `off` | never judge; the guards stay inert |

The model is TypeSafe System One, asked as a `noul` plus a `choice` with
confidence. A sure answer d

ecides; an unsure one falls back to the offline
detector; a failure of any kind falls back too. Noth

ing ever blocks a turn on a
network problem. Answers are cached by content hash, and prose sent upst

ream is
capped at 4000 characters.

The key comes from `TYPESAFE_AI_FABRICIO_KEY` (or `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) in the
environment, then from
the credential store.
## What the section says

The chat rule carries the verbatim list — code, commands, paths, identifiers,
error strings, tool ou

tput — so a forced prose language never translates a
payload. The artifact rule names every artifact

kind and exempts quoted user
text, untouched existing files, and localization resources that follow

quoted user
text, untouched existing files, and localization resources that follow their own
locale.
An explicit request for another language in one message wins for that turn only.
## Enforcement layers
| Layer | Surface | Effect |
| Reminder | `system-prompt/assemble` | the policy is restated in the runtime-context snapshot, whic

h sits at the tail of the request and replaces itself every step |
| Write guard | `tools/pre-execut
e` | before `write`/`edit` runs, the comments and documentation are checked; a wrong language denies

the call with a retry instruction, so nothing bad lands on disk |
| Summarizer | own `compaction` e
ngine | subclasses the stock engine, so every inherited step stays and only the directive gains the

artifact language |
| Title | `llm/stream` (`purpose: 'session-title'`) | the title follows the chat

nguage |
| Title | `llm/stream` (`purpose: 'session-title'`) | the title follows the chat language |

The summarizer is mounted from inside the plugin, not from a row, and only when
nothing else claims

`compaction`. A preset or a backend-mode jev is therefore
detected instead of crashing the boot; the

checkpoint just keeps the host
language. The stock row is disabled so it cannot race ours into the

service.
Everything inherited — range selection, replay prefix, envelope, usage
accounting — is unto
uched, and jev-compaction keeps pruning before the summary.

The write guard judges only human prose: documentation bodies and comment lines.
Identifiers, string

s, and data files are ignored, and so are localization
resources. A file with fewer than eight words

of prose is left alone. Every agent gets its
own budget: at most two denials and two corrections pe

se is left alone. Every agent gets its
own budget: at most two denials and two corrections per turn.
